source.title: Do LLMs Really Forget? Hidden-State Leakage in Model Unlearning and How to Fix it
source.authors: Hadi Reisizadeh; Jia-Jun Ruan; Si-Jia Liu; Ming-Yi Hong

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether output-level unlearning leaves recoverable information in hidden states and whether relearning and jailbreak attacks recover it. It also reports a new method intended to reduce that leakage.
record.gate_note: The paper reports hidden-state generative probing, fine-tuning relearning attacks, and GCG jailbreak attacks. It does not test quantization or prompt rephrasing without an attack. The probing figures report curves without extractable numeric values; the paper's text describes the trends. The theoretical analysis is also relevant to whether output suppression amounts to erasure.
record.test_reason: The study's own experiments bear on several versions. Fine-tuning on a forget-set subset for 75 steps tests B, generative probing of hidden states tests C, and GCG bears on E. PARS is a proposed robust counter-method, which bears on F. The paper argues output-level unlearning is an illusion of forgetting, which counts against A. None of the three original sources is this paper.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors' primary claim is that output-level unlearning creates an illusion of forgetting, shown in theory and by generative probing on TOFU, MUSE and WMDP. PARS, built on NPO, is offered as a first step that beats the baselines on MIA, Leak@k, relearning and GCG. The paper's claim of 'perfect forgetting' under ES on TOFU sits oddly with Table 3's PARS ES of 13.0.
record.recipe_differences: PARS adds an adversarial generative-probe objective at selected hidden layers to NPO-based unlearning; it is not the original unlearning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported probing results vary by benchmark, unlearning method, and layer. PARS uses selected intermediate layers, with TOFU layers {8, 10, 12, 14} and MUSE-News layers {24, 26, 28, 30}.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 1 shows that output leakage can be driven to zero while information about the sensitive variable stays in the representation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output suppression without representational erasure is theoretically possible. This is an existence argument, not a measurement.

fits_no_version.finding: Min-K%++ membership inference scores are reported for each method (Table 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Detection of memorization signal, not recovery of knowledge.

record.problems: The probing figures provide no extractable numeric values in the text. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper does not give a chance-level reference for the output metrics. The GCG tables do not provide a direct no-GCG unlearned value. The evidence is limited to the stated benchmarks and settings.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 and Table 4 also report multiple unlearning-effectiveness and utility values; only the PARS TOFU retain-utility result was included because of the 60-row limit. Other retain-utility values and the full output-level metric rows are omitted. The probing plots show additional original-model/control curves, which are omitted; exact plotted values are not stated.

untested.parts: No chance-level reference for the output metrics. Baseline utility values (e.g., the MUSE KnowMem Dr drop from 55.2 to about 41) are not in the rows.
Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data is not tested; only a forget-set subset is used.
No ablation of an activation direction; the evidence is generative probing only.
Rephrasing, other languages and in-context information are not tested. The GCG results lack a no-attack baseline, so recovery by jailbreak cannot be read.
PARS is not tested against quantization, prompt-only attacks other than GCG, or on WMDP.

missing.what: Leak@64 under repeated sampling: TOFU ES Original 84.3; GradDiff 80.5, NPO 75.9, SimNPO 76.4, RMU 96.7, PARS 73.7, despite single-shot ES of 13-22. MUSE RS Original 96.4 vs 80.6-93.2 for unlearned models. Sampling recovers most of the forgotten content.
Utility of baselines on MUSE: KnowMem Dr falls from 55.2 (Original) to 40.3-42.6. Baseline TOFU retain ES is 29.6-35.4.
Single-question example where probes at layer 28 recover the answer for NPO and SimNPO while outputs suppress it; the PARS probe fails.

record.verdict_notes: Row codes V1-V6 correspond to A-F; the GCG rows were wrongly linked to B. On TOFU the unlearned forget ES is not far below Original (e.g., 22.4 vs 26.7), so the near-chance premise of A is weak there. The probes are trained on 80% of the forget set, and no control probe on a never-exposed model is reported. Part of the probe recovery may therefore reflect what the probe itself learned. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not state a chance-level reference for its output metrics. It evaluates retain-set utility, but the full set of utility values is not extracted here.
The relearning attack fine-tunes on a small subset of the forget set for 75 steps; it does not test unrelated or loosely related examples.
It does not ablate an activation direction. It tests generative probing of hidden states and presents a theoretical argument about output suppression versus representation erasure.
The prompting attack tested is GCG jailbreak optimization. Rephrasing, other languages, and in-context information are not tested.
PARS is evaluated on TOFU and MUSE-News, including the reported relearning and GCG settings; the paper does not test quantization or prompt-only attacks other than GCG.

rows.subject: Theoretical model in Theorem 1
rows.operation_detail: Derived information-theoretic bounds for output leakage and information in hidden representations.

conditions.value: ε-insensitive decoder direction and Theorem 1 assumptions

rows.measure: Mutual information between sensitive variable and hidden representation/output
rows.value: I(S;R) lower bound depends on backbone; I(S;Z|C) upper bound is ε² Var(µS); the paper states output leakage can be zero while representation information remains positive.
rows.note: This is a theoretical result, not an empirical model evaluation.
rows.check: A theorem showing that suppression without erasure is possible is not an empirical measurement of any model. It should not be a row; it is moved to fits_no_version.
